headline: DocuSign profit surges as costs stay flat against growth
summary_short: Revenue rose 8.7% y/y to $830.2M as operating income jumped 84.7% to $111.3M and net income grew 8.5% to $78.2M, with diluted EPS of $0.40 up from $0.34 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew 8.7% y/y to $830.2M, led by commercial/enterprise and digital-channel expansion; international revenue rose 17% and reached 31% of total. Gross margin held flat at 79.4%. S&M (36% of revenue, down from 39%) and R&D (19%, down from 21%) grew roughly with revenue, lifting operating income 84.7% to $111.3M and operating margin to 13.4% from 7.9%. Net income rose 8.5% to $78.2M ($0.40 diluted EPS) despite a much larger tax provision ($39.6M vs $1.7M) tied to OBBBA-related tax law changes. Cash plus short-term investments were $814.2M; DocuSign repurchased $318.4M of stock and generated $289.4M of non-GAAP free cash flow. No numeric forward guidance appears in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth held steady while sales & marketing and R&D grew roughly in line with revenue rather than faster, so nearly all incremental revenue fell to operating income.
Increase was primarily due to expansion of revenue from commercial and enterprise accounts, as well as the digital channel; international revenue grew 17% and reached 31% of total revenue.
Cost of revenue, S&M, R&D and G&A all grew roughly in line with or slower than revenue (S&M and R&D both fell as a % of revenue), so operating margin expanded to 13.4% from 7.9%.

Net income grew slower than operating income because the income tax provision rose to $39.6M from $1.7M, driven by U.S./foreign earnings tax on stock-based compensation and OBBBA-related tax law changes.
EPS growth (+17.6%) outpaced net income growth (+8.5%) because diluted share count fell to 196.5M from 212.8M, reflecting the quarter's $318.4M of buybacks.
